name_en: Butaae — octopus and eggplant stir-fried in sweet miso, named for the pork it once stood in for
summary_ja: 茹でタコとなすを甘辛い麦味噌で炒め合わせた天草の家庭料理。かつて手に入りにくかった豚肉の代わりに、地元で獲れるマダコを使ったのが始まりとされ、名前だけ「豚和え」として残ったという。
summary_en: Boiled octopus and eggplant are stir-fried in a sweet, spicy barley miso — an Amakusa home dish said to have begun as a stand-in for pork, once hard to come by, using the local octopus instead while keeping the old name, "pork mix."

name_en: Kasuyose — coarsely ground soybeans stewed with root vegetables and chicken into rice
summary_ja: 一晩水に浸した大豆を粗く砕き、里芋やにんじん、鶏肉と一緒に米を加えてとろっと煮込んだ料理。山都町で祝い事や祭りの際につくられてきたとされ、主食にもおかずにもおやつにもなるという。
summary_en: Soybeans soaked overnight and coarsely crushed are simmered down with taro, carrot, chicken, and rice into a thick stew — said to have been made in Yamato for festivals and celebrations, serving as a main dish, side, or even a snack.

name_en: Yama surume no kinpira — sun-dried bamboo shoot strips stir-simmered sweet in soy
summary_ja: ゆでたたけのこを天日干しにした「山するめ」を水でもどし、千切りにして醤油や砂糖で炒め煮する料理。乾燥したたけのこがスルメに似て見えることが名の由来とされ、生とは違う食感が楽しめるという。
summary_en: Boiled bamboo shoots sun-dried into "yama surume" (mountain dried squid) are rehydrated, cut into strips, and stir-simmered in soy and sugar. The name is said to come from how the dried shoots resemble dried squid, offering a texture unlike fresh bamboo.
source_title: 山するめのきんぴら 熊本県

name_en: Ichimonji no guruguru — blanched leek greens coiled around their own white stalk
summary_ja: さっと茹でた一文字（わけぎ）の白根を軸に青い葉をぐるぐる巻きつけ、酢味噌や辛味噌をかけて食べる酒肴。肥後藩の倹約令の時代に考案された安価なつまみとされ、白根の膨らみが熊本の一文字の特徴という。
summary_en: The white base of blanched wakegi (a bunching-onion relative) is used as a spool for its own green leaves to coil around, then served with sweet or spicy vinegar-miso — said to have been devised as a cheap drinking snack during a Higo domain austerity edict.
source_title: 一文字のぐるぐる 熊本県

name_ja: 蛇腹大根（房切り大根）の煮物
name_en: Jabara daikon no nimono — accordion-cut dried daikon simmered with vegetables
summary_ja: 大根に切れ目を入れて蛇腹状に伸ばし、冬の冷たい風で干し上げた保存食を戻して煮る料理。南阿蘇地域の冬の風物詩とされ、干すことで旨味と栄養が凝縮し、パリっとした独特の食感になるという。
summary_en: Daikon is scored and stretched into an accordion shape, then dried in the cold winter wind of southern Aso into a keeping food — said to be a seasonal sight there — before being rehydrated and simmered, its dried texture crisp and its flavor concentrated.
source_title: 蛇腹大根（房切り大根）の煮物 熊本県

name_en: Hone kajiri — bone-in wild boar or pork simmered for hours and eaten by hand
summary_ja: 猪や豚の骨付き肉を水から3時間ほどじっくり煮込み、塩だけで味付けする料理。骨の髄まで吸って楽しむことからこの名がついたとされ、猟師料理がもとになったという奥球磨地域の宴会料理。
summary_en: Bone-in wild boar or pork is simmered from cold water for about three hours and seasoned with nothing but salt — named, it is said, for how everyone sucks the marrow from the bone, a banquet dish in Oku-Kuma said to trace back to hunters' cooking.
